findings.evidence: The Routines summary reads '1 total · 0 active · 1 draft', and the filter row offers all/draft/completed/archived with no Active filter or section, while the row says 'Plan: Draft' and the overview shows 'Next: Lower body · Week 2' after three logged weeks. 'New routine' is the only filled button; the existing plan's Open is an outlined control inside the row.
findings.userConsequence: A user who is already training this plan cannot tell what makes a routine 'active' or isolate one, and the page's strongest emphasis points at creating another routine rather than continuing.
findings.suggestedChange: Explain the plan state as 'Draft plan' with one line on what active means, add an Active filter or remove the active count until that state is reachable, and give the current plan's Open action weight closer to New routine.

findings.evidence: Prescription lines, History/More controls, and Library previews and counts use a subdued green-grey that is dimmer than the baseline dark capture opened for comparison. Text remains legible, but this tier sits closest to decoration and is weaker than the equivalent light-theme text.
findings.userConsequence: Prescriptions and catalog previews need closer reading at phone size, and the separation between task text and tertiary metadata is less clear than in the light theme.
findings.suggestedChange: Raise the secondary foreground one step in the terminal theme while keeping decorative counts subordinate, and recheck at 390px.

findings.evidence: The profile header ends with a bare pencil glyph at the far right, while the Body card below uses a labeled 'Edit' control with the same icon. These are the screen's only edit entry points.
findings.userConsequence: The name and summary edit action can read as decoration and be missed; a user may assume only the Body fields are editable.
findings.suggestedChange: Add a visible 'Edit' label to the header action or reuse the labeled Body pattern for both.

findings.evidence: The bodyweight card plots three marked points with date labels but no vertical scale or point values; the only numbers are in the caption (Starting 169 · Current 168 · Change −1 · Range 168–169).
findings.userConsequence: The line's slope can be over-read, and the chart adds little beyond the caption for a 1 lb change.
findings.suggestedChange: Add min/max axis labels or small value labels at the three points, keeping the point markers and honest nonzero scale.

findings.evidence: History rows end with 'last 10/26' for every recent movement, and the exercise-history sheet labels sessions 'Oct 26 (Mon)' and 'Oct 19 (Mon)' without a year.
findings.userConsequence: Once logs span more than one year, users cannot tell this October from last October when comparing sessions.
findings.suggestedChange: Include the year when it is not the current year, either in the row metadata or the session header.

findings.evidence: At the captured scroll position the sticky Back/Save program footer cuts across the Weekly preview: the third day card begins under the footer and no bottom clearance is visible. The two earlier day cards end cleanly above it.
findings.userConsequence: A user reviewing before saving may think only two days were imported or miss the third day's exercises.
findings.suggestedChange: Reserve footer-height bottom padding in the scroll area so a complete day card can clear the footer while the actions stay sticky.

strengths: Prompts puts Copy prompt with its character count and Go to Import above collapsed coach prose, so the offline copy/paste workflow is the first visible task.

The four import states are plainly differentiated: a counted JSON editor, a bordered recovery alert with Copy as primary, a gated Resolve step, and a confirmation that names the catalog link and says further review is optional.

Mobile workout now shows every exercise's set row in the first viewport with 15px set values, 13px prescriptions, labeled History and More, and a bordered rest-edit control; the saved 6/6 status and Finish workout action stay visible.
Routine overview names the next day and week, opens the week containing it, marks 'Next workout' in the list, and keeps analysis to a single summary row.
The desktop shell is stable: persistent sidebar, one content origin and measure, no duplicate hamburger; workout tools stay near exercise names and routine actions group with their row.
History rows now have real separators and trailing chevrons, explicit sort labels, and legible metadata; export filters stack to one column, counts are summarized, and Copy/Download remain clear.
Workspace surfaces Theme before the long storage explanation, keeps Download backup dominant, styles destructive import distinctly, and states local-first limits in plain language.
Light and dark captures share structure and semantics; navigation pairs consistent line icons with labels, and the session summary and onboarding each give one obvious next action.
limitations: Static 390x844 and 1280x900 captures only; keyboard, focus, screen-reader, tap-target, persistence and scrolling behavior were not tested.
Dark evidence covers four screens and desktop evidence four routes; other states at those themes and widths are unverified.
Contrast is a visual judgment only; no ratios were measured. The terminal-theme finding is a comparative visual impression.
Workspace's Request protection button and the remaining Appearance controls are below the fold in both themes, so their stated fixes cannot be confirmed here.
Warm-up 'Set rest' without a prescribed duration and the paired 'rest 90s' / '1:30' displays were treated as intentional data-driven states, not defects.
Baseline captures were reopened only for mobile workout, dark workout and mobile History comparisons; this was not a full image-to-image audit.
All 27 manifest files were present, hash-verified against the manifest, and opened directly as images.
Prior-round reviews, all four assessments and the round-4 implementation response were read; no other current-round output, source edits, app interaction or delegation occurred.
